content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification:** deviation (walk-away territory) — the agreement gives Customer no convenience exit in a three-year term, and Section 2.1 expressly negates termination rights during the take-or-pay commitment.

**What I inspected:** Section 9 in full (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/SLA/law/IP, 9.5 severability of Order Forms — no 9.4 exists), plus Sections 2.1, 6.2, 8.1–8.3, 10.2, 19.4 and 27.3. All other exits are cause-based; Section 8.2 is natural-term non-renewal (RENEWAL, not T4C, so not double-flagged). Vendor holds no convenience right today, but the preferred checklist requires that to be affirmative.

**Redline (preferred, validated ok:true):**
1. New Section 9.4 — Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on thirty days' written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
2. Section 2.1 — deleted only "or termination " so the take-or-pay clause no longer contradicts the new right; the volume-reduction restriction is preserved verbatim.
